title: Deadlock thaws: IndiGo, AI Express to start int’l flights from Navi Mumbai from Dec
content: In an exciting move, IndiGo is set to launch international flights from Navi Mumbai International Airport in February 2027. The airline aims to shift twelve daily international departures from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport to enhance travel connectivity. This strategic transition will also support the redevelopment of the existing airport.

title: Hyd techie found dead after threatening to take her life during video call to boyfriend
content: Archana Chowdhury Malik, a 29-year-old software employee, was discovered dead by hanging in Hyderabad. The incident occurred in an apartment located in Chandra Nayak Thanda. Police received information about her death and quickly arrived at the scene. Authorities have registered a case and are investigating the circumstances of her passing.

title: A taste of crocodile in Thailand lands Madhya Pradesh civic officer in hot water
content: A video has emerged featuring Ujjain Municipal Corporation officer Rajkumar Rathore and his wife sampling crocodile meat during their trip to Thailand. Rathore was on leave from October 19 to 23 but failed to inform anyone about his overseas travel. Municipal Commissioner Abhilash Mishra stated that officials must obtain permission for international journeys. The situation will be examined, and disciplinary measures may follow if rules were breached.

title: Eric Schmidt reveals his biggest failure as Google CEO
content: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt has called missing out on social media his biggest mistake as CEO. Speaking on the In Good Company podcast with Nicolai Tangen, Schmidt said Google was briefly ahead of everybody else before Facebook pulled away. He took responsibility for the miss, one that Orkut and Google+ could not fix, and admitted that being too slow was his biggest personal failing.

title: Israel elections: Can Netanyahu turn security gains into a political victory?
content: Israeli voters will head to the polls on October 27 in a significant election for Benjamin Netanyahu. His political future hinges on addressing security failures following the October 7 attack by Hamas. Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a primary challenger, emphasizing military accountability over Netanyahu's leadership. The election highlights divisions within the opposition and potential coalition challenges.

title: Canadian couple builds swimming pond for $52,000 after quotes hit $200,000
content: On their sprawling 65-acre property, Crystal Drinkwalter and Jazmyn Canning took on the ambitious project of building a natural swimming pond after being deterred by high contractor fees. Through hard work, they relocated more than 100,000 pounds of rock and lined the pond by hand. It took eight water trucks to fill their 110,000-gallon pond with water. For a detailed look at this impressive feat, visit their YouTube channel.

title: Elvish Yadav home firing, 58 cases: Why STF wants Himanshu Bhau back
content: Gangster Himanshu Bhau has been detained in the US, which may assist Haryana Police in extraditing him. He faces 58 criminal cases linked to violent gang activities in Rohtak and surrounding areas. Bhau allegedly runs an organized crime network responsible for killings, extortion, and illegal activities. Haryana's Special Task Force arrested numerous members of his gang, indicating ongoing efforts to tackle organized crime.

title: 'If it was up to me': Anderson admits Lancashire exit was not how he wanted it to end
content: Anderson expressed his disappointment in a social media post, writing: "I've supported Lancashire since I was a kid and so to get to play for them for 25 years was a dream come true.

title: After cardiac arrest, Damar Hamlin helps set record: 1,293 learn CPR in an hour
content: Damar Hamlin set a Guinness World Record by successfully teaching hands-only CPR to 1,293 individuals at Acrisure Stadium. This event, part of a broader initiative in partnership with the American Heart Association, aimed to raise awareness about cardiac emergencies and emphasize the importance of immediate response. Fueled by his personal experience with cardiac arrest, Hamlin sought to empower his community with life-saving skills for potential emergencies.

title: Veterans seek court order to block Trump's 250-foot arch before Nov 5
content: US President Donald Trump's proposed 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington could begin construction as early as November 5, pending final approvals. However, three military veterans and a retired architectural historian have asked a federal judge to stop the work, arguing that congressional authorisation is required. The project faces two lawsuits questioning its approval process and legality.

title: Nasa’s Isaacman shares Artemis IV update as SpaceX, Blue Origin plan Moon base
content: NASA administrator Jared Isaacman provided an update regarding the Artemis III lunar mission and upcoming docking exercises. The agency plans for significant interactions with Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin next year. Docking practices will involve astronaut teams launching aboard NASA's Orion capsule from Cape Canaveral. Isaacman indicated that the competition has intensified due to historical precedents set by earlier space missions.

title: Florida buyer's condo unfinished after $1.65m deposit; $418m foreclosure suit
content: Nilesh Undavia and other buyers are struggling to receive their deposits for unfinished luxury condos in Boca Raton. The Mandarin Oriental Residences project has faced significant construction delays, impacting buyers' financial investments. A $417.7 million foreclosure lawsuit complicates the situation for prospective homeowners seeking refunds. Penn-Florida Companies attributes delays to various challenges, including rising construction costs and supply-chain issues.

title: First Indian ever! Deepti Sharma scripts history with century against Zimbabwe
content: In a remarkable display of skill, Deepti Sharma secured her place in history with an unbeaten century against Zimbabwe in Vadodara. Achieving the milestone in just 83 balls, she struck 15 boundaries, demonstrating her batting prowess from the No. 6 position. Furthermore, Harmanpreet Kaur's impressive 126-run innings added fuel to the fire, as they forged a record partnership, propelling India to a formidable total.

title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million estate faces opposition over landscaping plans
content: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh delays as neighbors challenge his landscaping and fencing plans. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.

title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany's KC Current extend unbeaten home run to 31 games
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ Kansas City Current have secured their third consecutive NWSL playoff berth after Portland’s 1-0 win over North Carolina. The club now aims to secure home-field advantage ahead of the postseason. Despite roster changes, Kansas City has maintained a record 31-game unbeaten home streak. Temwa Chawinga leads the team with 12 goals, while Croix Bethune has recorded 10 assists heading into the decisive final matches.

title: US midterms: From immigration reform to $15 minimum wage, all about Pramila Jayapal
content: Pramila Jayapal is gearing up for her re-election campaign in Washington’s 7th Congressional District. She will compete against Republican Nirav Sheth, who prioritizes public safety and addresses homelessness issues. Jayapal champions healthcare, immigration reform, and tackling economic inequality. Notably, she broke barriers as the first South Asian American woman in Congress back in 2016. The election is slated for November 3, with both candidates actively promoting their visions.

title: Daler Mehndi row: Minister refuses to back down; says, 'Look, we didn’t even start it'
content: In a dramatic live performance in Tehri, a confrontation unfolded between Punjabi singer Daler Mehndi and Minister Subodh Uniyal. Uniyal accused Mehndi of lip-syncing and alleged he was under the influence, igniting outrage among the music community who rallied behind Mehndi. Following the escalating dispute, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami stepped in to mediate, while Mehndi has remained notably silent amid the uproar.

title: Shaheen Afridi surpasses Akhtar, becomes fastest Pak pacer to reach ODI milestone
content: Bowling first, Shaheen dismissed England opener Tom Banton in the first over to claim his 150th wicket in the 50-over format. The 26-year-old became the second-fastest Pakistani bowler overall and the fastest Pakistani fast bowler to reach the landmark.

title: Nayanthara gets 60-foot cut-out installed for ‘Mookuthi Amman 2’
content: Nayanthara is poised to reprise her iconic role as the goddess Amman in 'Mookuthi Amman 2', hitting theaters on November 6. A stunning 60-foot cut-out of her has been unveiled at Vels Theatre, marking this momentous occasion in Tamil cinema. Co-star Regina Cassandra has lauded Nayanthara for her significant contribution.

title: Kochi: 55-year-old man killed as judge’s minor son rams luxury car into scooter
content: A 55-year-old man named Jayabalakrishnan died after a luxury car collided with his scooter in Kochi. The minor driver, a 17-year-old, is the son of an Additional District Judge. The police have detained the teenager and registered a case for reckless driving and causing death by negligence. Initial investigations indicate that the minor was not under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident.

title: Yuki Bhambri wins Almaty Open; triumph offers boost after medal-less Asiad
content: Bhambri and Seggerman won 7-6(3), 6-7(1), [10-2] to secure the ATP 250 title and give Bhambri his fifth career doubles crown on the ATP Tour.

title: ‘Nuclear threat will overshadow all’: Netanyahu’s Iran warning ahead of polls
content: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has issued a stark warning about the looming Iranian nuclear threat. Analyst Yuval Blumberg emphasizes the urgency of the next two years for Israel to take decisive measures. He cautioned against letting internal political matters overshadow critical national security issues, especially with the parliamentary election approaching on October 27. Trump's support of Netanyahu further solidifies their alliance as essential in addressing Iran's ambitions.

title: BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
content: On Sunday, four Pakistani fishermen were intercepted by the Border Security Force in the Kutch district of Gujarat. Suspected of illegally fishing in Indian waters for crabs, they were detained following precise intelligence alerts. The crew members, hailing from Chach Jaan Khan village in Sindh province, are now under investigation as the BSF maintains vigilance over the sensitive border region to thwart unauthorized entries.

title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after protests over hydropower project
content: The Centre has deployed two Rapid Action Force companies comprising around 250 CRPF personnel to Arunachal Pradesh following violent protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. A mob torched an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, injuring over 40 police personnel. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam, faces opposition from indigenous tribes fearing displacement and submergence of villages.

title: India wants to become a global talent hub. What needs to change?
content: Returning professionals are just one part of a wider flow of talent. Indians are coming back after years abroad. Members of the diaspora are sharing specialist knowledge from where they are. International experts are arriving for a defined period to build skills and pass them on. The pull is increasingly professional. India now hosts 2,117 global capability centres employing 2.36 million people, according to the Nasscom-Zinnov GCC Landscape 2026.

title: What’s Delhi breathing? IITM’s new lab decodes air mix
content: Real-time data from the new Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory highlights various pollution contributors. Vehicles were the largest contributor to Delhi's PM2.5 pollution at 25%. Secondary organic and inorganic aerosols also significantly contributed to pollution levels across the city. This facility, inaugurated by Union minister Jitendra Singh, aims to identify and assess pollution sources.

title: 'This is Sachin, this is Dravid': How Manvanth Kumar fell in love with cricket
content: Karnataka all-rounder is finding his feet in domestic cricket with batting, bowling and ability to deliver under pressure. From his father's love for Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid to the influence of Manish Pandey and coaches Yere Goud and Vinay Kumar, Manvanth reflects on his journey, ambitions, workload management and his love for anime.

title: Toxic foam returns to Yamuna as AQI touches 168, GRAP-1 restrictions in force
content: The air quality in Delhi-NCR has substantially deteriorated, with the Air Quality Index registering an alarming 168, indicating unhealthy conditions. Toxic foam has resurfaced on the Yamuna River, particularly around Kalindi Kunj. In response, the Commission for Air Quality Management has initiated Stage 1 of the Graded Response Action Plan.

title: Tensions flare in Hyderabad after eggs 'thrown' at idol during procession
content: Hindu organisations protested following an incident where eggs were allegedly thrown at a Durga Mata idol. The incident occurred during an immersion procession within Madanapet police station limits in Hyderabad. Police responded promptly after receiving a call and took the suspects into custody for investigation. A similar incident involving stone-pelting was reported during a Durga Visarjan procession in Maharashtra.

title: Why India’s answer to China’s mega dam is facing resistance in Siang valley
content: In Arunachal Pradesh, the ambitious 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project has ignited fierce resistance from local tribes. They express fears about the potential displacement of over 150,000 residents and the loss of villages and farmland. While state officials assert that the pre-feasibility report is merely an early assessment, indigenous communities voice discontent over unauthorized survey actions and urge a reevaluation of the initiative.

title: Cancelled flight tickets: Airlines can claim GST refunds if fare and tax are returned
content: The GST Appellate Tribunal ruled that airlines are eligible for GST refunds on cancelled flight tickets. Singapore Airlines was allowed to reclaim Rs 45.92 lakh after proving refunds were issued directly to passengers. The tribunal emphasized that airlines must provide ample documentation to establish the refund trail. This decision affects eight claims spanning from October 2019 to March 2021 amidst the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: ‘VIP culture’ in hospitals can compromise patient safety, equitable care: AIIMS doctors
content: Pressure from influential patients can lead to unnecessary medical procedures and a longer recovery time for others. Surgical oncologists at AIIMS Delhi emphasize that this practice undermines equal treatment for all patients. Prolonged hospital stays for VIPs can also negatively impact hospital resources and staff morale. The authors advocate for appropriate clinical protocols and transparent admission criteria to ensure fair patient care.

title: India, Australia troops train for coastal, island warfare in AUSTRAHIND 2026
content: Indian and Australian army troops are actively participating in joint combat drills at the Foreign Training Node in Thiruvananthapuram, designated Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026. This exercise, featuring approximately 240 servicemen including 120 from each country and a New Zealand observer team, is crafted to boost operational synergy with specialized activities such as combat swimming, ambush strategies, and focused aerial operations aimed at refining skills for joint coastal and island maneuvers.

title: Protests engulf Europe: People take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal
content: Thousands of people protested across Europe over the weekend, demanding action against rising living costs and government corruption. Demonstrations were reported in France, Italy, Albania, Spain, and Portugal, with varying degrees of violence. Clashes between protesters and police resulted in numerous arrests and injuries in several countries. Many demonstrators called for affordable housing, better education, and protection of public pensions.
